\title{Sparse Attention Routing for Long Documents}
\author{A. Author \and B. Author}
\begin{document}
\maketitle
\begin{abstract}
We study sparse attention routing. Our method reduces memory by 40\% on long inputs while keeping accuracy within 0.5 points.
\end{abstract}
\section{Introduction}
Long documents are expensive to process because attention is quadratic in sequence length. \lipsum[1-2]
\section{Related Work}
\lipsum[3]
\section{Method}
\subsection{Routing Network}
The router assigns each token to one of 16 buckets using a learned projection. \lipsum[4]
\subsection{Training}
We train the router jointly with the language model for 20k steps. \lipsum[5]
\section{Experiments}
On the LRA benchmark our model reaches 61.2 average accuracy compared to 60.7 for the dense baseline. \lipsum[6-7]
\section{Limitations}
We only evaluate English text and models below 1B parameters. The router adds training instability at high learning rates.
\section{Conclusion}
